correctness.rationale: Normalize b=B/K and f(z)=log(1+z^h). For 0<h<=1, strict Jensen concavity gives unique all-n equal positive doses. For h>1, f′ increases then decreases; if a stationary maximum had unequal positive x<y, f′(x)=f′(y), then f″(x)+f″(y)>0 by (h-1)sinh((h+1)t)>(h+1)sinh((h-1)t), contradicting maximality along feasible pair transfer. Thus every global maximizer is equal on exactly k positive entries, with objective F_k(b)=k log(1+(b/k)^h). The function g(u)=log(1+u^h)/u increases up to unique u_h then decreases, where h u_h^h/(1+u_h^h)=log(1+u_h^h). For consecutive k, F_k=F_(k+1) crosses exactly once θ_k in (k u_h,(k+1)u_h); disjoint consecutive brackets imply θ1<...<θ_(n-1), no skipped support or nonadjacent tie, first θ1=2(2^h-2)^(1/h). A direct independent root calculation for h=2,3 reconstructed ordered adjacent thresholds and exact first threshold. Domain all real h>0, n>=2, identical positive K and total B, no toxicity/interaction constraints. Finite root checks supplement the analytic proof.
